concepts.name: Grouped Frequency Distribution
concepts.description: Grouped data organizes observations into class intervals along with their corresponding frequencies. This representation simplifies the analysis of large datasets.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to organize raw data into grouped frequency distributions and identify class intervals, class marks, and frequencies.

concepts.name: Arithmetic Mean of Grouped Data
concepts.description: The arithmetic mean represents the average value of grouped data and is calculated using class marks and frequencies. It provides a measure of the central tendency of the dataset.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the arithmetic mean of grouped data using the direct method.

concepts.name: Assumed Mean Method
concepts.description: The assumed mean method simplifies calculations by selecting a convenient reference value and computing deviations from it.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine the mean of grouped data using the assumed mean method.

concepts.name: Mode
concepts.description: The mode is the value or class that occurs most frequently in a dataset. For grouped data, it is estimated using the modal class and a standard formula.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the modal class and calculate the mode of grouped data.

concepts.name: Modal Class
concepts.description: The modal class is the class interval having the highest frequency. It serves as the basis for estimating the mode of grouped data.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the modal class from a grouped frequency distribution.

concepts.name: Applications of Mode
concepts.description: The mode is useful in identifying the most common or frequently occurring value in practical situations such as market research and surveys.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to interpret the mode in real-life contexts involving grouped data.

concepts.name: Median
concepts.description: The median is the middle value that divides an ordered dataset into two equal parts. For grouped data, it is estimated using the median class and interpolation formula.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the median of grouped data using the standard formula.

concepts.name: Median Class
concepts.description: The median class is the class interval that contains the median value of the grouped data. It is identified using cumulative frequencies.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine the median class using cumulative frequency.

concepts.name: Cumulative Frequency
concepts.description: Cumulative frequency is the running total of frequencies across class intervals. It is essential for locating the median class.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to construct cumulative frequency tables and use them to determine the median.

concepts.name: Measures of Central Tendency
concepts.description: This chapter summarizes the methods for determining the mean, median, and mode of grouped data. These statistical measures help describe the central value of a dataset.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to select and apply the appropriate measure of central tendency for grouped data in mathematical and real-world situations.
